title: Creep and Superalloys
description: Hot enough, any metal flows like slow honey under load: creep. A turbine blade runs a few hundred kelvin below its melting point for years, so it is cast from nickel superalloy, strengthened by tiny cubes of a second phase, and grown as a single crystal so no grain boundary can slide. Larson and Miller found that temperature and time trade together: a few percent hotter costs most of the life. Unlocks the Bridgman Furnace.

puzzle.goal: Larson and Miller: P = T·(C + log₁₀ t) is the same for every test at one stress. Write the rupture life t at temperature T.
puzzle.name: Larson Miller life
puzzle.ask: Find t in hours for P = 26000, C = 20 and T = @{T} K.
puzzle.method: Divide by T, take away C, and undo the logarithm.
